subject: Human Evolution
title: The Taung Child
description: A quick, practical guide to The Taung Child.

hook.text: In 1924, a small skull arrived on Raymond Dart's desk in South Africa—a child's face, but not human.

buildup.text: Dart identified it as Australopithecus africanus: a bipedal ape with a brain smaller than a chimp's.

discovery.text: The Taung Child was the first australopithecine ever found—proof that upright walking came before big brains.

twist.text: British scientists rejected Dart for decades. They were invested in the Piltdown hoax pointing to England.

climax.text: By the 1950s, more African finds vindicated Dart completely, and Piltdown was exposed as a fraud.

punchline.text: A child's skull humbled an empire's pride.

quiz.question: What did the Taung Child prove?
